title: Shipping fee
prompt:
Gadget Gulch ships repaired gadgets home. Replace the line `fee = 12` with an `if`/`elif`/`else` chain that follows the rules in the comments.

When it works, `python3 shipping.py` prints `Shipping: 7`. The tests try light, heavy and member parcels, including exactly 1 kg and exactly 5 kg.
hints: The member rule has two parts that must both be true. Which word joins them?
Put the member check first, then the light parcels, then the middle ones. The first true branch wins.
`if member and weight < 5:` sets `fee = 0`; then `elif weight < 1:` sets 3; `elif weight < 5:` sets 7; `else:` sets 12.
explain_after: `and` joins two conditions, and it short-circuits: when `member` is `False`, Python does not even look at the weight [py-060]. `elif` is short for else if [py-058], and the chain runs only its first true branch. A 0.5 kg parcel also passes `weight < 5`, so the `weight < 1` branch has to come first.
